In my opinion this is out of scope here, the main purpose of lilipod is to serve as container engine rather than an image builder. The problem with implementing this feature is that it will open the window for more new features which are out of context here, this should be clear at the start.

Anyway, I can see a problem using [imagebuildah](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/containers/buildah/imagebuildah); from my experience, it requires a [standard image storage](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/containers/storage#Store), which lilipod does not offer. If I am correct, this requires lilipod to setup another storage to be used just for those builds.
I agree, building is a bit too far off of the project

`getsubids` is available from `uidmap_1:4.13`@`bookworm` but not before (in `uidmap_1:4.8`@`bullseye` for example).
I've this little pure bash script `getsubids.sh` compiled with `shc` in `.local/bin/getsubids` which do the job :
```
#!/bin/bash
# shc -vrf getsubids.sh -o getsubids
re="^$USER:"
index=0
while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]
do
  [[ $line =~ $re ]] &&
    echo "$index ${line//:/ }" &&
      exit 0
  index=$((index+1))
done < /etc/subuid
exit 1
```

If this is a systemd-based system then you don't modify folder permissions but instead let systemd manage and provide elevated privileges. It's probably out of the scope of lilipod to do this for you given it's meant to be a bare-bones container manager but some documentation in the README for setting up systemd services would be great.

I think it is related to [AppArmor](https://ubuntu.com/blog/ubuntu-23-10-restricted-unprivileged-user-namespaces), missing a /etc/apparmor.d
